file_roles.evidence: qt_GetMessageHook tested the hook's wParam for equality, '&& wp == PM_REMOVE && d->sendPostedEventsTimerId == 0', so when Windows passed PM_REMOVE|PM_NOYIELD the branch was skipped and the posted-events timer was never started. The fix reads it as a bit field, 'const bool messageRemoved = (wp & PM_REMOVE) != 0;' used as '&& messageRemoved &&'. The equality test is the wrong logic and this file owns the delivery of posted events.

rationale: The reporter sees an embedded window that 'no longer refresh (unless during a resize), and no longer receive any input event', which is posted events never being delivered, and the commit explains the mechanism, 'Windows unexpectedly passes PM_NOYIELD flag in wParam parameter to the hook procedure'. The diff changes exactly the condition that decides whether to arm the delivery timer, from '==' to a mask test. The missed branch and the undelivered events are in the same file.
notes: The report names a culprit commit rather than a location, 'I've narrowed down the problem to this commit: QEventDispatcherWin32: fix posted events delivering', which happens to land on the gold file. The user-visible surface is a QWinWidget-embedded window from the separate qt-solutions repository, which is outside the snapshot and has no frame in the packet, so symptom_location records the project-owned site. No log or trace was pasted. The packet says the fix changed 2 files of which 1 is non-test source, so a test did ship with this fix.
